title.en: How far apart are two points?

text.en: Two friends stand at different points of a school ground drawn on a grid. How far apart are they? The distance formula answers using only coordinates.

Every point on the plane has coordinates (x, y), measured from the origin along the x-axis and y-axis.
The distance between P(x1, y1) and Q(x2, y2) is the square root of (x2 - x1) squared plus (y2 - y1) squared.
This comes from the Pythagoras theorem on a right triangle with horizontal side x2 - x1 and vertical side y2 - y1.
The distance of a point (x, y) from the origin is the square root of x squared + y squared.
Example: distance between (2, 3) and (4, 1) is the square root of 4 + 4 = root 8 = 2 root 2.
To check that three points are collinear, show that the sum of two of the distances equals the third.
To identify a triangle: three equal sides - equilateral; two equal - isosceles; Pythagoras holds - right-angled.
To identify a quadrilateral: equal sides and equal diagonals give a square; equal opposite sides and equal diagonals give a rectangle.

problem.en: Check whether the points (1, 5), (2, 3) and (-2, -11) are collinear.

text.en: AB = root(1 + 4) = root 5, BC = root(16 + 196) = root 212, AC = root(9 + 256) = root 265.
Compare: root 5 + root 212 is not equal to root 265.

why.en: No two add up to the third.

text.en: So the points are not collinear.

why.en: Collinear points need a sum match.
